subject: [PATCH] rhashtable: specialize default comparison for constant parameters

2026-10-02.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the default comparison function in the Linux kernel's rhashtable module by utilizing compile-time constants when possible, reducing the need for dynamic memory access and improving performance. The patch achieves this by passing constant parameters from the caller to the comparison function, allowing it to use scalar comparisons instead of the generic memcmp() function. This change is expected to improve performance in various areas of the kernel, including scheduling, networking, and file systems.
